target.title: Fix nodejs installation logic on Debian-based systems
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on Debian-based systems who have the `pacman` arcade game package installed would experience a broken Node.js installation flow because the installer incorrectly routes them through the Arch-based `pacman` package manager path instead of `apt`/NodeSource.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous logic used a loose OR (`||`) condition: `command -v pacman || is_arch_linux`. 

On Debian-based systems, a package named `pacman` (the arcade game) exists in the official repositories. If a user has it installed, `command -v pacman` succeeds. However, because `is_arch_linux` also had a fallback that returned success if `pacman` was in `$PATH`, changing the operator alone was insufficient. 

To fix this reliably, we:
1. Made the Arch distro predicate independent of the `pacman` binary by checking only system identity files (`/etc/os-release` and `/etc/arch-release`).
2. Enforced both condition checks (`&&`) in the installation branch so that we only target Arch systems that actually run `pacman` as their package manager.

## User Impact

Users with the `pacman` game installed on Debian/Ubuntu/Mint can now install Node.js cleanly via the official installer without it crashing or attempting to invoke `pacman -S`. Arch-like distributions continue to install Node.js via `pacman` as expected.

## Evidence


### Follow-up (optional)
Dear maintainers,
If you agree, I can send a separate PR to add explicit helpers like `is_debian_linux()` and `is_fedora_linux()` and use them to improve distribution detection for `install_node()` and other needed processes.
